_comment: Tier-2: SlidingCableElement3D3N REQUIRES CONSTITUTIVE_LAW on Properties — its Init() errors by name if it is missing, unlike RingElement and EmpiricalSpringElement which read properties directly. Pitfall (kratos.cable_net #6, edge 1 of three). Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image). With YOUNG_MODULUS, DENSITY and CROSS_AREA set but no law, Initialize raises 'Error: A constitutive law needs to be specified for the element with ID 1'; adding SMA.TrussConstitutiveLaw() — the 1D law the claim recommends — makes the same Initialize succeed. Only edge 1 of this three-part claim is covered; edges 2 (mIsCompressed silent zero-stiffness) and 3 (FRICTION_COEFFICIENT Capstan sliding) need a converged multi-step solve and are named in the report as not yet done. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics at module scope; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 builds the SlidingCable WITH its CONSTITUTIVE_LAW, the documented requirement the fixture omits, so Initialize succeeds instead of raising. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS and these expect_in_output strings disappear: initialize_without_law_raised=True, observed=constitutive_law_needed_for_element, sliding_cable_law_mismatches=0. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/cablenet_sliding_cable_requires_constitutive_law && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (fails). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
